label: VERIFIED
extraction: Anthropic criteria for when multi-agent provides value. Multi-agent architectures provide value when they address specific constraints single agent cannot overcome: 1) Single agent accumulates everything in context (must reason about technical issue while maintaining 20+ files), 2) Parallel workstreams with independent context, 3) Specialization single agent can't sustain. Observed teams invest months building elaborate multi-agent architectures only to discover improved prompting on single agent achieved equivalent results. Common failure modes: lost context at each handoff, spent more tokens coordinating than executing. Decision framework: reserve multi-agent for cases where they provide clear benefits justifying additional cost. Managed infrastructure can handle orchestration (Claude Managed Agents). Patterns: generator-verifier, orchestrator-subagent, agent teams. Key principle: multi-agent should be reserved for cases with clear benefits justifying cost.
